rationale: Made visible by #398 rather than caused by it. `mergedConfiguration` is SYNTHESIZED by both CLIs, so an empty value there is a computed default rather than authorship information — which is exactly why `drop_absent_optional` still runs on BOTH sides of that block and why #398 retired it only on `configuration`. Until #398, deacon emitted its own empties there too and the rule absorbed the difference symmetrically; now deacon omits them and the reference does not, so the difference has a direction and is recorded here instead of being only compensated. Measured at oracle 0.87.0 for `{"image": "alpine:3.19"}`: the reference emits `remoteEnv: {}`, `containerEnv: {}`, `portsAttributes: {}` and `hostRequirements: {cpus: null, memory: "-Infinity", storage: "-Infinity"}`; deacon emits none of the four. The two documents describe the same merged configuration — no consumer can act differently on an absent `containerEnv` than on an empty one — so the divergence is tolerated rather than treated as a defect to rush a fix for. The `hostRequirements` values in particular are upstream's `Math.max()` over an empty set serialized as the strings `"-Infinity"`, and reproducing that shape uncritically would be adopting a quirk, not achieving parity. Self-invalidates the moment the difference stops reproducing.
